topics.title: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO following Trump intervention
topics.explanation: Nvidia's board reversed its previous decision and reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as chief executive officer after intervention from President Trump. Huang had previously resigned following an acknowledgment of an extramarital affair. His return triggered a massive rally in Nvidia stock, adding nearly $1 trillion in market value.
topics.why_it_matters: Nvidia is central to the global artificial intelligence industry, so leadership stability and executive changes at the company directly move broader stock markets.

topics.title: Sanofi agrees to acquire Insmed for $41 billion in major pharma deal
topics.explanation: French pharmaceutical company Sanofi has agreed to buy US biotech firm Insmed for $41 billion. The acquisition represents the pharmaceutical industry's largest deal in three years and expands Sanofi's rare-disease and immunology pipeline. Insmed's shares surged 14% following the announcement.
topics.why_it_matters: Major drugmakers use acquisitions to bolster product pipelines and replace revenue lost when top-selling medicines face generic competition.

topics.title: CrowdStrike to buy cybersecurity firm Zscaler for $44 billion
topics.explanation: Cybersecurity provider CrowdStrike announced an agreement to acquire competitor Zscaler in a $44 billion transaction. CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz defended the deal as a strategic move to address evolving digital security threats. The deal comes as corporate cybersecurity demand expands to counter AI-driven attacks.
topics.why_it_matters: Consolidation among major technology suppliers can reshape industry competition and security infrastructure choices for global enterprises.

topics.title: COP31 climate summit ends without deal following fossil fuel disputes
topics.explanation: The United Nations COP31 climate conference concluded without a consensus agreement for the first time since 2009. Negotiations collapsed after participating nations failed to agree on financial aid commitments for developing nations and language regarding fossil fuels. The failure leaves future global energy transition policy frameworks uncertain.
topics.why_it_matters: International climate policy outcomes influence long-term government regulation and global investments in renewable energy and traditional fossil fuels.

topics.title: Fed watchdog probes Governor Michelle Bowman over quiet period dinner
topics.explanation: The Federal Reserve's internal watchdog has launched an investigation into Federal Reserve Governor Michelle Bowman. The inquiry focuses on whether Bowman violated central bank blackout rules by speaking at a private Bank of America client dinner shortly after a policy meeting. Fed rules prohibit public comments during designated quiet periods surrounding interest rate decisions.
topics.why_it_matters: Strict ethics and communication rules at the Federal Reserve maintain public trust and prevent market-moving hints from leaking to private investors.

topics.title: Germany's business confidence improves for seventh straight month
topics.explanation: The Ifo Institute reported that German business expectations improved for a seventh consecutive month, suggesting Europe's largest economy is stabilizing. However, Ifo President Clemens Fuest warned that long-term structural issues will slow growth after 2026. Growth is projected at roughly 1.3% for the current year before decelerating.
topics.why_it_matters: Germany is Europe's largest economy, making its industrial and business health a key indicator for broader European economic growth.
